title: Evaluation investment has visible upfront cost and deferred benefit, so it is chronically under-provisioned
problem: I know I should build evals before scaling my agent, but the cost lands this sprint and the payoff lands in a quarter I cannot point at.
symptom: Teams ship agents on manual testing and intuition, then hit a wall where they cannot tell a regression from noise and have no way to verify a change except to guess.
why_now: Agent quality is now the top barrier to deployment while eval tooling remains a per-team build. The economics are understood and still lose to delivery pressure, which makes this an adoption gap rather than a knowledge gap.
existing: Eval frameworks and hosted platforms: reduce build cost but still require a task bank the team must author.
Production monitoring: catches issues after users do.
Golden transcripts: cheap to start, brittle as the agent legitimately changes behaviour.

evidence.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents (Anthropic Engineering)
evidence.quote: Their compounding value is easy to miss given that costs are visible upfront while benefits accumulate later.
evidence.note: The same post names the failure state precisely: 'Absent evals, debugging is reactive: wait for complaints, reproduce manually, fix the bug, and hope nothing else regressed.' Date is the publication month listed by the publisher.

build_hypothesis: Derive the first eval bank from artefacts the team already has - production traces and closed bug reports - so the upfront cost is a script run rather than an authoring project.

check.manual_question: This project calls a model API. Where is the eval suite that tells you a prompt or model change did not regress behaviour?
check.rationale: An agent codebase with no eval directory and no eval test has no way to distinguish a regression from noise. Directory presence is a weak but honest proxy, and a false positive here costs one MANUAL answer.
